intelligence.title: Intelligence profile
intelligence.tooltip: Each score combines several metrics, converted to percentiles within the comparison group first, then weighted. A score of 0–100 says where this player sits on that composite — not how good they are.
intelligence.description: Composite scores built from contextual percentiles.
intelligence.relativeNote: Expressed relative to comparable players, not as a measure of quality.

roles.title: Role compatibility
roles.tooltipLabel: Raw Role Fit and Role Fit Percentile
roles.tooltip: Raw Role Fit is the weighted statistical profile score, built from the components listed below it. Role Fit Percentile is where that score stands among every player evaluated for the same role. Roles weight their components differently, so raw scores from two roles are not directly comparable — the percentile is, and it is what the best role is chosen by. Metric Coverage, shown when it is below full, is the share of the role's configured weight backed by metrics the provider actually supplies; missing components are left out rather than counted as zero. None of the three is player quality.
roles.description: Statistical fit against each role compatible with this position.
roles.percentileOf: {percentile} percentile of {population} evaluated for this role
roles.partialNoPercentile: Role fit percentile not available for partial role definitions.
roles.meaning: Role score measures resemblance to a profile.

whyRole.title: Why {role} = {score}
whyRole.description: Every component that produced the score, and what each contributed.

performance.title: Performance
performance.tooltipLabel: What does a percentile mean here?
performance.tooltip: A 94th percentile means this player comes out better than 94% of the comparison group on that metric. Higher is always better here, whichever way the metric runs: a player who is rarely dispossessed reads high, not low. Where that flips the reading, the rank by raw value is printed underneath. The comparison group is stated below the table and is never hidden.
performance.globalNote: The second column ranks the same figures against all {population} players in this position across every loaded competition. Neither column is adjusted for how strong a league is, because this system does not model that: a player high at home and lower here has not been judged worse, they have been placed in a bigger population. Which number matters is a recruitment decision, not a statistical one.
